source_read: PMC full text PMC4547584 (Public Health Rep 2015;130(4):339-342), read in the app's browser in my own tab: the whole commentary (12 running-text paragraphs, the four-item indicator list, the figure title and both footnotes, acknowledgements, affiliations and 9 references). The page structure was checked with a script for the paragraph locators. The single figure (a JPG chart) is figure image not viewable: I scrolled it into view and loaded it (727x375), but the screenshot and a zoom of my tab both came back blank because the pane is hidden. The image has no alt text or long description with values, so only values printed in the text were checked, and no figure value was estimated. Card check only (the task lists no claims); I read the source and noted my own observations before opening the card. No funding or competing-interests statement is on the page.

key_findings.correction: The 7th paragraph describes the MCOD files as compiled from certificates 'for U.S. citizens'. The card does not carry this; see missed.

All values printed in the 8th paragraph match. The Kansas and Michigan comparison (more unspecified than opioid-analgesic deaths) can only be checked against the figure, which I could not view either.
Ranking, total rates and stable specification are in the 10th paragraph; checking ME, coroner and toxicology records is in the 11th.

reporting_issues.note: Same limitation in my reading: figure image not viewable.

Re-found independently (no T40.1 indicator despite the heroin claims in the 1st and 2nd paragraphs). The 2nd paragraph does introduce the system-type percentages with 'the degree of underestimation varied'.
Neither the article page nor the expanded author information carries one.

risk_of_bias.note: JBI prevalence with an overall 'moderate' fits the certificate-data comparison. Domain 4 'no' is justified: the argument turns on certification practice, which is not described for the 11 jurisdictions.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor: the undercount statements are hedged in the text and the practical advice follows from the data. The card rightly notes that heroin is claimed but not analysed.

missed: 11th paragraph: the commentary cites the 2013 recommendation of the National Association of Medical Examiners and American College of Medical Toxicology expert panel that certifiers list all substances responsible for a fatal overdose, and the 2013 SAMHSA uniform definitions. It says that until these are consistently adopted, counts should be read with caution where the share of unspecified deaths is considerable. The 12th paragraph adds that NCHS and some states were working to improve drug specification. Neither is a key finding, though both bear on how deaths are certified.

7th paragraph: the MCOD files are described as covering certificate data 'for U.S. citizens'. NCHS mortality files are by residence, so this is probably a slip (from my own knowledge, not stated in the source; to be confirmed). The card's population description should not repeat 'citizens'.

selection_effects says the authors 'work in the health departments of the jurisdictions they describe, including the first author's Kentucky'. The first author is at the University of Kentucky College of Public Health (Kentucky Injury Prevention and Research Center), not a health department, as the card's own affiliations_note says; the other ten are at health departments.
